transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-06-25
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Aisha Malik (CTO - Sundial.io), Jon Reyes (Head of ML), Priya Nair (Infra Lead)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): PLG quickstart discovery. Customer interested in fast time-to-first-token, wants to compare hosted vs dedicated vs private for ML infra. Security and data residency are potential blockers.

00:00:00 Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — i'm Maya, i'm the AE on this account, and Ethan is our SE. can you do quick intros from your side?
00:00:12 Aisha Malik: Hi all, i'm Aisha, CTO at Sundial. We run a small team building conversational routing and analytics. We're exploring Redwood for inference, mainly to ship a beta quickly.
00:00:23 Jon Reyes: Jon here, head of ML. i'm curious about latency and cost tradeoffs — we have token-heavy summarization pipelines.
00:00:30 Priya Nair: Priya, infra lead. main constraint is VPC-only egress and strict KMS policy. We also need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM.
00:00:45 Ethan Park: Great — thanks. i'd like to spend the first 10 minutes understanding your current stack and success criteria, then walk through quickstart options.

00:01:10 Jon Reyes: Quick context: currently using a mix of hosted APIs for prototyping and self-hosted GPUs for larger batches. We're evaluating whether a hosted Redwood API could be used for prod, or whether we need Dedicated or private deployment behind our VPC.
00:01:30 Maya Chen: Perfect. what's your time-to-first-token expectation — like, from signup to call? are you optimizing for dev speed or total cost?
00:01:40 Jon Reyes: Dev speed first. If we can get a working token in under an hour and do a few sample calls that's ideal. Cost matters for production, but early phase it's less important.
00:01:52 Aisha Malik: Also important — we have to show security compliance to our procurement folks. SOC 2 or ISO things — do you have docs?
00:02:05 Ethan Park: Yes, we have SOC 2 and ISO docs. we'll share the pack after the call. For quickstart we offer self-serve sign up, SDKs, and free credits to run your first calls. Typical time-to-first-token is 5-20 minutes if you follow the quickstart.
00:02:26 Priya Nair: Can that quickstart be done within our VPC? Our networking requires traffic stay in VPC and we prefer a private endpoint.
00:02:36 Ethan Park: For initial evaluation, hosted is easiest — you sign up, get API key, and hit the endpoint. If you need VPC-restricted access, Dedicated or our Private deployment is the route — Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and private network peering, Private is full VPC/on-prem control. There's usually a bit more setup for private — typically a week to onboard for a simple VPC peering setup, longer if air-gapped.
00:03:05 Jon Reyes: Sounds good. Any quick notes on latency; our SLA target is sub-200ms p50 for short chats and sub-1s for summarization with 1k tokens.
00:03:18 Ethan Park: For hosted, our verified profiles show 80-180ms p50 on smaller models depending on region and sequence length; for dedicated you get more predictable p50/p95 depending on instance sizing. We can run a 1-hour benchmark to show expected latency.
00:03:35 Aisha Malik: That benchmark — does it require access to our data? We prefer not to upload sensitive logs.
00:03:42 Maya Chen: We can run synthetic workloads or use an encrypted upload. But we also support private deployments where data never leaves your network. For hosted evals we have strict data retention and can sign a data processing addendum if needed.
00:03:58 Priya Nair: How about KMS integration? Our encryption keys are in AWS KMS and we need to control key lifecycle.
00:04:07 Ethan Park: We do KMS integrations and can support customer-managed keys for Dedicated and Private. For hosted we can do bring-your-own-key in select enterprise tiers — i'll include details in the security pack.

00:05:00 Jon Reyes: On quickstart — do you have SDKs and code samples for node/python and a sample that shows streaming responses and function calling?
00:05:10 Ethan Park: Yes, SDKs in python/js, and the quickstart repo includes streaming example and function/tool calling. Usually a developer can get a demo running in 10-15 minutes. We'll link the repo in the follow-up.
00:05:24 Maya Chen: We also give free credits for new orgs to run a pilot. For this pilot we can provision $2k in credits good for 30 days.
00:05:33 Aisha Malik: That's helpful for dev speed. What's the friction to switch to Dedicated later? Are model versions compatible?
00:05:42 Ethan Park: It's designed to be smooth — same API surface. You can pin model versions and route by policy. Migration from hosted to Dedicated is typically a config change plus capacity provisioning; we help with rollout.

00:06:05 Priya Nair: One thing — our procurement insists on audit logs and token-level billing exports. Does Redwood expose per-token billing and traces?
00:06:16 Maya Chen: Yes — Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and tracing hooks. We can also stream audit logs to your SIEM via a connector.
00:06:28 Jon Reyes: Competitors we looked at: OpenAI for convenience, Anthropic for safety stance, and Replicate for self-hosted models. Two main tradeoffs are latency predictability and cost.

00:06:45 Ethan Park: Exactly — Redwood tries to give deterministic economics: batching, KV cache (sometimes transcribed as K-V cash), quantization profiles to lower token cost while keeping quality. If you want we can propose a quantization profile for your summarization workload.

00:07:10 Aisha Malik: For pilot success criteria — we'd want 1) working integration in our staging, 2) p50 latency under 250ms for interactive flows, 3) a cost estimate vs self-hosting. Timeline is roughly 3-6 weeks for pilot.
00:07:26 Maya Chen: That's reasonable. Proposed plan: quickstart first week (signup + free credits + simple call), week 2 run benchmark and measure latency/cost, week 3 decide on Dedicated trial or Private assessment.

00:07:45 Jon Reyes: Ok — what do you need from us to start the quickstart?
00:07:50 Ethan Park: Just an email to create the org for the trial. We can also send invite links so your devs can sign up themselves. We'll provide step-by-step for time-to-first-token.
00:07:59 Priya Nair: Also i'll send our network constraints and whether a private endpoint is a hard requirement for staging.

00:08:10 Maya Chen: Great. i'll set up the trial org and apply the $2k credits. Ethan i'll make sure the se checklist and bench scripts get to Jon.

00:08:20 Ethan Park: quick notes on bench script: it'll run small chat workloads, summarize a 1k-token doc, and measure p50/p95 with and without KV caching. Also measure throughput for batching. We'll provide instructions for using your own keys or synthetic data.

00:08:45 Aisha Malik: For security pack, include SOC 2, encryption at rest/in transit, KMS support, SSO/SAML, RBAC. Our procurement will want that up front.
00:08:56 Maya Chen: Yep — we'll attach the security pack and an architecture note showing options: hosted (fast), Dedicated (peered, reserved), Private (VPC/on-prem, longer lead).

00:09:10 Jon Reyes: One more technical: do you support model catalog and comparing open checkpoints? We want to test 7B and 13B variants and measure latency vs cost.
00:09:20 Ethan Park: Yes — our catalog shows curated open models with performance profiles. We can recommend quantization-friendly variants for throughput. For model switching we'll help with rollouts.

00:09:36 Priya Nair: Do you have per-route rate limits and quotas? We need to protect the production endpoint.
00:09:43 Maya Chen: Console allows rate limits, quotas, and automatic fallback policies. You can set per-key or per-route limits.

00:10:00 Aisha Malik: Ok that's helpful. Let's recap and next steps.
00:10:05 Maya Chen: Recap: Redwood will provision trial org + $2k credits, Ethan will share benchmark checklist and quickstart links, Redwood will share SOC2/security pack and architecture note. Sundial will send infra diagram and confirm if private endpoint is required for staging. We'll tentatively schedule a 60 minute performance check-in next week — Aisha will confirm availability.
00:10:30 Jon Reyes: Sounds good. Any blockers on our side? Priya will check network constraints and i'll coordinate devs for quickstart.
00:10:40 Priya Nair: i'll send the network constraints by EOD Monday.

00:10:50 Maya Chen: Great — action items noted. Thanks everyone.
00:11:00 Aisha Malik: Thanks, talk soon.

(Transcript: some words auto-transcribed slightly off; e.g., "K-V cash" for KV cache in one spot. Minor crosstalk around 00:05:40.)
